texts.facts: This writ petition has been filed challenging the proceedings initiated by the first respondent in No.4723/2023/A dated 24.01.2024, on the compliant lodged by the respondents 2 & 3 under Sections 5 & 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizen Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as the Act). 2. The petitioner is the daughter of the respondents 2 & 3 herein and she got married one Velmurugan. Before her marriage, her entire family had been in the real estate business in the name and style of Sri SPK Real Estate. A partnership deed was entered into between the petitioner and her parents and brother on 18.06.2003 and they had purchased several properties in the name of the firm. Apart from the said firm, they have a school in the name of SPK Matriculation Higher Secondary School and Sri SPK Public School (CBSE) in Tiruchengode. Both the schools were managed by a trust called SPK Educational Trust, in which the petitioner was a trustee and managing director. 3. While being so, there was an interse dispute between them https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and therefore a memorandum of understanding was executed on 15.07.2015 among the family members. Pursuant to which, the petitioner had resigned from the trusteeship and the post of managing director and relinquished her rights. Upon her resignation, her brother and sister-in- law were inducted as new trustees in the trust. As per the memorandum of understanding, some of the properties were settled in favour of the petitioner by the respondents 2 & 3 by the registered settlement deeds dated 12.10.2015, registered vide documents Nos.6585, 6587, 6590, 3352, 6403 & 6404 of 2015. 4. Thereafter, there was a dispute between the petitioners and her family members resulted in so many writ petitions and registration of FIRs. Therefore, the respondents 2 & 3 lodged complaint by invoking provision under Section 3 & 23 of the Act and the same has been taken cognizance by the first respondent. Hence, the petitioner filed the present writ petition with the above prayer. 5. Though the first condition has been fulfilled, the respondents 2 & 3 failed to fulfill the second conditions. As per the settlement deed, there is no specific clause that the petitioner shall maintain the respondents 2 & 3 till their life time. The respondents 2 & 3 lodged complaint to cancel the settlement deeds executed in favour of the petitioner on 12.10.2015 vide document Nos.6585, 6587, 6590, 3352, 6403 & 6404 of 2015.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the complaint can be maintained by fulfilling two conditions as per https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Section 23(1) of the Act. The first condition is that, the settlement deeds should have been executed after coming into force of the Act and the second one is, it should contain a specific clause imposing an obligation on the settlee or transferee to maintain settlor or transferor. 5.1. In support of his contention, he relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sudesh Chhikara Vs.
